findings.evidence:
Screenshot shows the entire admin order-detail page rendered at very low opacity (near-invisible: navbar, order header, dropdowns, totals all faded). Root cause identified by reading resources/css/app.css:336-337 — `.backdrop { opacity-0 ... transition } .backdrop.active { opacity-100 }` is a page-wide semi-opaque (bg-black/60) overlay shared by every `.dropdown-group` (declared once at the top of BackendNavbarComponent.vue: `
`). The capture fires immediately after `Promise.all([page.waitForResponse(...), paidOption.click()])` resolves, with no wait for the backdrop's CSS transition to finish closing after the dropdown selection — so the snap() caught mid-fade. This is a test-capture-timing artifact (one animation frame), not a real production rendering defect: functional correctness is proven independently by the DB-level assertions (after.pos_payment_method, after.payment_status, after.fiscal_sequence_no), and a real cashier would never see this half-second transitional frame as a static state.
findings.fix_hint: Optional spec polish only: await a short `page.waitForTimeout(350)` or `.dropdown-group:not(.active)` state before snap('01-...') if a crisper screenshot is wanted for future visual-diff baselines. Not blocking.

attack_log.attack: 1. Re-verify '.dropdown-group .dropdown-btn' text-scoped-by-"Non payé" selector genuinely disambiguates from navbar
attack_log.method: Read resources/js/components/layouts/backend/BackendNavbarComponent.vue in full (lines 1-130) — 4 dropdown-btn buttons exist: branch selector (text = branch.name), language switcher (text = language.name), a router-link with dropdown-group class but no dropdown-btn class (KDS shortcut), and the profile menu (text = 'Bonjour ' + user name). None render fr.json label.unpaid ('Non payé', fr.json:784) or label.paid ('Payé', fr.json:783) anywhere, including no notification badge with that text. Also read OnlineOrderShowComponent.vue (the actual page) — 3 dropdown-group elements exist there: delivery-boy assign (hidden, order_type!=DELIVERY for this TAKEAWAY fixture), payment-status (button text = paymentStatusEnumArray[order.payment_status], target), order-status (button text = orderStatusEnumArray[order.status], distinct enum, never 'Non payé'). Selector is provably unique on the page.
attack_log.verdict: CONFIRMED REAL — the fix is a genuine disambiguation, not cosmetic.

attack_log.attack: 2. Verify PosMethodFromGateway::appliquer() guard at line 71 is real, and the fixture genuinely starts pos_payment_method=NULL
attack_log.method: Read app/Services/Payments/PosMethodFromGateway.php in full — `if ($order->pos_payment_method !== null) { return; }` is real, unconditional guard code (not a docblock claim). Read app/Services/OrderService.php:2638-2870 (changePaymentStatus) — confirms the call site `app(PosMethodFromGateway::class)->appliquer($locked)` at line 2868, placed right after `$locked->save()` seals PAID, inside the same locked DB transaction. Checked database/factories/OrderFactory.php — no `fiscal_sequence_no` or `pos_payment_method` default is set anywhere in the factory (grep returns zero hits for fiscal_sequence_no in the factory file), and the spec's seedUnpaidCardOrder() explicitly overrides `pos_payment_method => null`. The spec's own test additionally re-reads the fixture from the DB (readOrderPaymentColumns, not a cached model) BEFORE acting and asserts `before.pos_payment_method` is null and `before.payment_status` is UNPAID(10) — this is a genuine pre-condition check baked into the test, not merely claimed in a comment.
attack_log.verdict: CONFIRMED REAL — guard exists, fixture genuinely starts NULL, the test exercises the actual overwrite-guard-bypass path (order.pos_payment_method WAS null, so appliquer() actually writes CARD(2)).

attack_log.attack: 3. Is the fiscal_sequence_no assertion doing real work, or could it already be non-null before the mark-paid action?
attack_log.method: Read app/Services/OrderService.php:2803-2814 — fiscal_sequence_no allocation for this exact code path (`$targetPaymentStatus === PAID && $locked->fiscal_sequence_no === null && ...`) happens INSIDE changePaymentStatus() itself, at seal time, not at order creation. Confirmed database/factories/OrderFactory.php's definition() never sets fiscal_sequence_no (nullable column per migration 2026_04_22_000001, no DB default). The fixture is created via Order::factory()->create() with status=ACCEPT (not PAID), so no other seal point (POS create OrderService:1117, confirmCounterPayment PaymentService:335-337, kiosk TPE FrontendOrderService:1232 — none of which this fixture's creation path touches) would have allocated a sequence number ahead of time. No OrderObserver auto-allocates it either (grep for an OrderObserver touching fiscal_sequence_no returns nothing).
attack_log.verdict: CONFIRMED REAL — the assertion measures an actual NULL-to-non-NULL transition caused by this test's own action, not a pre-existing value.

attack_log.attack: 4. Re-derive the CashDrawerService.js historical bug and confirm the current fix genuinely includes variance_reason in the outgoing payload
attack_log.method: Read `git show 53b1dc6d6 -- resources/js/services/CashDrawerService.js resources/js/components/admin/cash/PosCashDrawerSessionDialog.vue` — the diff shows closeSession() previously posted `{}` (literal empty body, confirmed by the removed comment 'body: {} (calculates expected + variance server-side)') to /reconcile, discarding the `varianceReason` parameter entirely. The fix changes the call to `const reconcileBody = varianceReason ? { variance_reason: varianceReason } : {}; ... client().post(.../reconcile, reconcileBody, ...)`. Traced the wiring further upstream: PosCashDrawerSessionDialog.vue:229 binds `v-model="varianceReason"` on `[data-testid=cash-session-reason-input]`, submitClose() (line 521-536) dispatches Vuex action `cashDrawer/closeSession` with `varianceReason: this.varianceReason || null` (line 530), and the Vuex module (resources/js/store/modules/cashDrawer.js:129-138) passes it straight through to CashDrawerService.closeSession(). Full chain from typed input to network body is real code, not a partial/cosmetic patch.
attack_log.verdict: CONFIRMED REAL — this is a genuine bug-fix, and the wiring from the reason `<textarea>` to the POST body is intact end-to-end.

attack_log.attack: 5. Does state 02a reach the 422 via a page.request bypass that could mask a UI-level regression?
attack_log.method: Read PosCashDrawerSessionDialog.vue:225-257 — the real submit button has `:disabled="loading || varianceReasonMissing"`, and varianceReasonMissing (line 405-408) requires the trimmed reason to be >= 3 chars whenever varianceRequiresReason is true. This makes it structurally IMPOSSIBLE to click a real UI submit button with an empty/short reason when a reason is required — so testing the empty-body 422 guard necessarily requires an API-level bypass; there is no UI path that could exercise it. State 02b (the very next test, same describe block) DOES drive the full real UI path — real click on `[data-testid=cash-session-open-submit]`, real `.fill()` on the reason textarea, real click on `[data-testid=cash-session-close-submit]` — and asserts the actual `page.on('request')`-captured network body. Between the two tests, both the client-side guard (02a implicitly, via reading the disabled logic) and the server-side guard (02a explicitly) and the real UI wiring (02b) are each independently proven.
attack_log.verdict: CONFIRMED REAL — 02a's page.request bypass is the only viable way to exercise this specific guard (the UI cannot reach it), and it does not substitute for the real-UI proof, which 02b independently supplies.
